title: 555 astable — flashing red and green LEDs

steps.title: The chip
steps.circuit: Start with the chip. Draw the 555 as a box and write each pin number where its wire will meet it. Those numbers are what you convert later.

steps.title: Supply rails and supply pins
steps.circuit: Draw +5 V along the top and 0 V along the bottom. Pins 8 and 4 (Reset) go to +5 V and pin 1 goes to 0 V. Pin 5 is left open.

steps.title: The timing parts: R1, R2 and C1
steps.circuit: R1 runs from +5 V to pin 7. R2 runs from pin 7 to pins 6 and 2, which are joined. C1 runs from there to 0 V, + side up.

steps.title: The two LEDs
steps.circuit: From pin 3, R3 and the red LED go down to 0 V. From +5 V, R4 and the green LED come down to pin 3.

steps.title: Test points
steps.circuit: T1 +5 V, T2 0 V, T3 the output (pin 3), T4 the capacitor (pins 2 and 6).

question.title: 555 astable — flashing red and green LEDs

seq.title: Place the chip
seq.lead: Start with the chip. Fit a socket for the 555 with the notch at the top, so pin 1 is top left, and cut the four tracks between its two rows (red ✗). Now every pin has a track of its own.
seq.how: Then work round the chip: its supply pins first, then the rest one pin at a time. Each pin's net goes in the track that pin is already in.

prompts.text: Where is pin 1? Tap it on the board.

items: 0 V supply lead: track B, at the top-left corner beside the other supply lead, so both can share one spiral wrap to the power supply.
A black link joins track B to track V. Both are net 2.
A black link joins track F (holes 1–13) to track V. Both are net 2.
seq.title: Pin 1: Ground (0 V) → net 2
seq.lead: On the diagram, pin 1 joins 0 V, C1 and LED1. Number it: net 2. Net 2 is the 0 V supply.
seq.how: Pin 1 is in track F (holes 1–13), so that track is net 2.

items: +5 V supply lead: track A, at the top-left corner beside the other supply lead, so both can share one spiral wrap to the power supply.
A red link joins track A to track I (holes 1–13). Both are net 1.
A red link joins track A to track F (holes 15–37). Both are net 1.
seq.title: Pin 4: Reset → net 1
seq.lead: On the diagram, pin 4 joins +5 V, R1 and R4. Number it: net 1. Net 1 is the +5 V supply.
seq.how: Pin 4 is in track I (holes 1–13), so that track is net 1. Pin 8 is on net 1 too, so its track joins in.

items: C1 goes in now, from net 4 (track U) to net 2 (track V).
A yellow link joins track G (holes 1–13) to track U. Both are net 4.
A yellow link joins track H (holes 15–37) to track U. Both are net 4.

prompts.text: C1 joins net 4 to net 2. Tap where its other leg goes.

seq.title: Pin 2: Trigger → net 4
seq.lead: On the diagram, pin 2 joins R2 and C1. Number it: net 4.
seq.how: Pin 2 is in track G (holes 1–13), so that track is net 4. Pin 6 is on net 4 too, so its track joins in.

seq.title: Pin 3: Output → net 5
seq.lead: On the diagram, pin 3 joins R3 and LED2. Number it: net 5.
seq.how: Pin 3 is in track H (holes 1–13), so that track is net 5.

items: R1 goes in now, from net 1 (track A) to net 3 (track G, holes 15–37).
R2 goes in now, from net 3 (track G, holes 15–37) to net 4 (track J).
A yellow link joins track H (holes 15–37) to track J. Both are net 4.

prompts.text: R1 joins net 3 to net 1. Tap where its other leg goes.

seq.title: Pin 7: Discharge → net 3
seq.lead: On the diagram, pin 7 joins R1 and R2. Number it: net 3.
seq.how: Pin 7 is in track G (holes 15–37), so that track is net 3.

items: R3 goes in now, from net 5 (track O) to net 6 (track R).
LED1 goes in now, from net 6 (track R) to net 2 (track S).
A black link joins track S to track V. Both are net 2.
A blue link joins track H (holes 1–13) to track O. Both are net 5.

prompts.text: R3 joins net 6 to net 5. Tap where its other leg goes.

seq.title: Net 6: R3 and LED1
seq.lead: R3 and LED1 meet away from the chip. Number it: net 6.
seq.how: Give net 6 a free track: track R.

items: R4 goes in now, from net 1 (track K) to net 7 (track N).
LED2 goes in now, from net 7 (track N) to net 5 (track O).
A red link joins track I (holes 1–13) to track K. Both are net 1.

prompts.text: R4 joins net 7 to net 1. Tap where its other leg goes.

seq.title: Net 7: R4 and LED2
seq.lead: R4 and LED2 meet away from the chip. Number it: net 7.
seq.how: Give net 7 a free track: track N.

seq.title: Test points
seq.lead: Mark a test point on each net you will measure, before you build.
seq.how: T1 on net 1, T2 on net 2, T3 on net 5, T4 on net 4.

seq.title: Check it against the diagram
seq.lead: Read the board back one track at a time and compare it with the numbered nets.
seq.how: Every net must be one track, or tracks joined by a link, and no two nets may touch. On the layout this earns the marks for no errors, annotation, track cuts and test points.

mistakes.title: Board A
mistakes.why: Right. The red LED's long leg is on the 0 V track and its short leg on R3's track. It is reverse biased, so it never lights. The green LED still flashes.

options.t: The red LED is the wrong way round
R3 is on the wrong tracks
options.fb: R3 runs from pin 3's track to the red LED, as it should. Look at the LED's flat edge.

options.t: The black link to 0 V is missing
options.fb: The black link from the LED's track to 0 V is there. Check which way round the LED is.

options.t: The green LED is the wrong way round
options.fb: The green LED is fitted correctly. Compare the two LEDs.

mistakes.title: Board B
mistakes.why: Right. The yellow link from track G to track U is missing, so pin 2 is joined to nothing. Pin 2 must be on net 4 with pin 6 and C1's + leg.

options.t: Pin 2 is not joined to C1 and pin 6

options.fb: R1 (1 kΩ) is from +5 V to pin 7 and R2 (10 kΩ) from pin 7 down, as drawn. Follow net 4: pin 2, pin 6 and C1.
All four cuts are there. Follow net 4 on the diagram: pin 2, pin 6 and C1+ must all be joined.

options.t: C1 is the wrong way round
options.fb: C1's + leg is on the timing track. Look for a missing yellow link.

mistakes.title: Board C
mistakes.why: Right. R2's top leg is in track H (pin 6) instead of track G (pin 7). R2 now joins net 4 straight to +5 V, and pin 7 has only R1.

options.t: R2 starts on pin 6's track instead of pin 7's

options.fb: R1 reaches from track A to pin 7's track. Look at where R2's top leg sits.

options.t: The yellow links are the wrong colour
options.fb: Colour doesn't change the circuit; the wiring is the problem. Look at R2's top leg.
The red link to pin 8's track is there. Check R2 against net 3 on the diagram.

quiz.q: Why are four tracks cut under the 555?
o: So the pins opposite each other are not joined
Right. Without the cuts, pin 1 would join pin 8, pin 2 pin 7, and so on.
To stop the chip overheating
The cuts are about which pins are connected, not heat. Which pins share a track without them?
To make room for the socket
The socket fits on uncut tracks too. Think about pin 1 and pin 8 on the same track.
Because the chip uses 4 V
The cuts have nothing to do with the voltage. Count the pins on each side of the chip.

quiz.q: R1 is drawn between +5 V and pin 7. On stripboard it must sit…
o: Across two tracks: one with +5 V, one with pin 7
Right. Each leg goes in its own net's track.
Along one track
Both legs on one track short the resistor out. Each leg goes in its net's track.
Under the chip
Parts never go under the chip. Find the +5 V track and pin 7's track.
Across the cut
The cuts are for the chip. Put each leg in its net's track.

quiz.q: When should test points be marked on the layout?
o: Before the board is built
Right. They are part of the plan, with the reading you expect beside each.
After it is soldered, where it is easy to reach
Test points added afterwards are not planned. Mark them on the layout first.
Only if the circuit doesn't work
Test points are planned for every board. They make testing quick.
Never on stripboard
Stripboards take test pins too, and the marking scheme expects them.
